structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E047. The tip is E036 (5.314 s; seeds 0–2 at 0.7532). Population mean is about 0.7525–0.7535, and each build plus seeds 0–2 counts as one draw with an SD of about 0.2 pp. A neutral change passes the 0.753 gate about 40% of the time.

Mechanism I hold that others under-weight: step time is conv compute plus a large, roughly fixed tail. That tail is per-parameter optimizer work (renorm, bf16 Newton-Schulz, foreach copies, Lookahead lerps) and memory-bound BN/activation traffic. Freezes beat FLOP accounting because they delete that tail as well as the backward FLOPs.

Consequences for this round:
- The I075 cascade is the best risk-adjusted lever. E046 saved about 10 ms per frozen step at no detectable accuracy cost, and a 0.25-epoch top-up costs about 0.13 s.
- ReLU (I078) mostly will not speed up the fused BN/activation kernels. They are bytes-bound, and GELU's erf is nearly free inside fused kernels. Meanwhile ReLU costs real accuracy on CIFAR-100 short runs.
- The deep extra conv in I077 adds a 512×512 Muon matrix, so the hidden optimizer tail grows along with the compute.
- On the accuracy side, the end of the run is robust to annealed freezes. It is fragile to changes in the objective, the averaging, or the activation function.

forecasts.reason: The 0.25-epoch top-up is worth about +0.08 pp of population mean, which a 20-seed pairing barely resolves (SE about 0.07 pp). Expect s/pp around 1.5–2.
E046's freeze saves about 0.235 s and the top-up costs about 0.13 s, giving a net of about −2.1%. Annealed freezes have been accuracy-neutral.
Only about 60–90 ms of the 135 ms of non-step work is removable, because interpolate and gathers remain. If the math stays identical, accuracy is just rebuild noise.
Conv compute plus an extra 512×512 Muon NS and BN/GELU adds about 3%. The capacity gain is probably smaller than the dial rate.
The fused kernels are bytes-bound, so ReLU saves only about 1–2%, short of the 3% threshold. ReLU typically costs 0.3–0.5 pp in short airbench-style CIFAR-100 runs.

cruxes: What share of a 32 px step is per-parameter optimizer work plus Lookahead (Muon renorm, NS, copies)? If it is ≥20%, batched or fused NS across same-shape filters is the next accuracy-free time lever.
In the same-build 20-seed pairing, is the group-2 freeze (I075 vs I074) within 0.05 pp? If so, extending the cascade (group-2 freeze from 85%, group-3 partial) dominates the epoch dial.
Does I074 measure the post-freeze dial at ≤1.5 s/pp? That sets whether any booster such as I077 can beat simply adding steps.
